preamble: Diphthongization of the long high front vowel /iː/ into a centring diphthong [iə] (written ie in this atlas, as for German ie [iə]) is a rare change. It is currently under way in West Frisian: speakers born after about 1980 increasingly pronounce /iː/ as [i·ə], especially before alveolar consonants, which merges it with the old phoneme /i·ə/. Earlier claims that this is a common cross-linguistic change were unsupported.

examples.note: Younger speakers realize /iː/ as the centring diphthong [i·ə], most often before alveolar consonants, so wiid becomes homophonous with wiet /vi·ət/ 'wet'; acoustic data from 51 Boarnsterhim speakers show the change increasing with later birth year.

sources: Kingma, M., Boersma, P., Van de Velde, H., & Versloot, A. (2023). Diphthongisation of /iː/ in West Frisian. Proceedings of the 20th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, 3005–3009. https://www.fon.hum.uva.nl/paul/papers/2023-icphs-KingmaBoersmaVeldeVersloot.pdf
